## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` → shared `householdId` feature for `POST /api/owners`.

**Behavior:** When a request sets `sharesHousehold: true` and another owner already shares the same last name and address (matched case-insensitively, whitespace-collapsed), the new owner is allowed (no 409) and both the new owner and existing household members are stamped with the same stable `householdId`, which is returned on `GET /api/owners/{id}`. The id is derived deterministically from the normalized last name + address (`HH-<12 hex>`), so all members of a household converge on the same value.

**Changes:**
- **`openapi.yml`** — added read-only `householdId` to the `Owner` schema (generates `OwnerDto.householdId`; mapped automatically by MapStruct, mirroring `customerCode`).
- **`model/Owner.java`** — new `householdId` field (`household_id` column) with getter/setter.
- **DB schemas** — added `household_id` to `owners` in hsqldb/h2/mysql/postgres `schema.sql`, plus a trailing `NULL` on the 10 positional seed rows in `db/hsqldb/data.sql` (the tests run on hsqldb; h2/postgres seeds use explicit column lists and were unaffected).
- **`OwnerHousehold.java`** (new) — shared helper: `normalize`, `sameHousehold`, and the stable `id(...)` derivation (SHA-256 based).
- **`CheckOwnerHouseholdUnique.java`** — refactored to use the shared helper; still throws 409 when `sharesHousehold` is false.
- **`AssignHousehold.java`** (new) — after `BuildOwner`, stamps the shared id on the new owner and back-fills existing household members lacking one. If nobody else is in the household, the id is left null.
- **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted the `assignHousehold` step (under `transaction` governance) between `build` and `assignCustomerCode`.

The `sharesHousehold` field remains write-only (never returned), per the existing spec.
